clue.text: Poet is country person admitting blunder

indicators.note: to admit something is to let it in, so one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: a hick is an unsophisticated rural person
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A poet turns out to be a rustic who lets a mistake slip in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country person' is a yokel here, not a citizen of some nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Herrick was a seventeenth-century English lyric poet, author of 'Gather ye rosebuds while ye may'.

clue.text: Stare at end of spectacle — then you shout audibly

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the last letter of spectacle
ye is the archaic plural you

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so we want a word that sounds like the one meant

parts.note: to bawl is to shout, and it sounds the same as a round toy

explanation.surface: Someone gawps at the climax of a show and then cries out.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is informally to look hard at them, a confrontational stare.

clue.text: Record in rubbish put in new container

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: An old record thrown in the bin ends up in a new box.
explanation.definitionFit: To repot a plant is to move it into a different pot, a fresh container for its roots.

clue.text: Workers at last having right to remove stones

indicators.note: the right letter is to be taken away from the word

parts.note: a last is the foot-shaped block on which shoemakers work
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Labourers finally get permission to clear away rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' looks like 'finally'; a last is the shoemaker's foot-shaped form, so its workers are COBBLERS, less R.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobbles are rounded stones used for paving streets, so they are stones by another name.

clue.text: Stay away from child sent to bed on time

parts.note: a boy is a male child
a cot is a small bed
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A parent's bedtime routine: the child is packed off to bed on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: The bedtime picture hides a plain run of pieces, child then bed then time.
explanation.definitionFit: To boycott something is to refuse to deal with it or attend it as a protest, which is staying away.

clue.text: Medical problem making one gutted — then made worse

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, so the middle letter goes

parts.note: taken as written before its middle goes

indicators.note: something made worse is damaged and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An illness that leaves a patient gutted and then deteriorates further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' reads as upset; here it removes the N from the middle of ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedema is swelling caused by fluid collecting in body tissue, a medical condition.

clue.text: For body tissue eat garlic misguidedly?

indicators.note: doing something misguidedly means getting it wrong, so the letters go astray into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dubious health tip: eat garlic to strengthen your body tissue.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the advice is misguided as well as the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartilage is the firm, flexible connective tissue found in joints, ears and the nose.

clue.text: One's quick on foot

parts.note: surface reading: someone who is a fast runner
setter's reading: the quick is the tender flesh under a nail, and this one sits on a foot

explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' reads as fast; the setter means the sensitive flesh beneath a nail, as in 'cut to the quick'.
explanation.definitionFit: Each nail on a foot has its quick underneath it, so the thing whose quick is on the foot is a nail of the toe.

clue.text: Degree of moderation?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an academic award such as a university degree
second meaning: a limiting or softening of a statement

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase asking how moderate something is; split it into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a certificate gained by study and a reservation that tones down or restricts a claim.

clue.text: Dickensian character — follower, not leader

indicators.note: the leader is the front letter, and 'not' tells us to drop it

parts.note: a sheep is someone who follows the crowd

explanation.surface: A Dickens figure described as a hanger-on rather than a ringleader.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the S from the front of SHEEP. Fittingly, Heep is a fawning creep, though not a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Uriah Heep is the obsequious, scheming clerk in Dickens's novel David Copperfield.

clue.text: Feature of tsar — I establish frontiers

parts.note: a word that features in a phrase is bound up inside it
the star sign sits inside these words, straddling the gaps between them

explanation.surface: A tsar boasts that marking out his empire's borders is his particular trademark.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer describes the wordplay, so the solver must notice the star sign sitting inside 'tsar I establish' and say how it sits there. 'I establish' wants to be the tsar talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Boundaries are the lines marking the limits of an area, which is what frontiers are between countries.

clue.text: Political alliance has yesteryear's president changing sides ultimately

indicators.note: the sides are right and left, and 'ultimately' points at the final letter, which swaps one for the other

parts.note: Jimmy Carter was US president from 1977 to 1981

explanation.surface: A past president switches his political loyalties at the last minute to join a coalition.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of CARTER is R for right; swap it for L, left.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartel is an association of parties or firms acting together, and in politics a bloc of allied groups.

clue.text: Honey going round Paris splashing the cash

indicators.note: going round suggests turning back on itself, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: mel is honey, from Latin, still used in pharmacy

indicators.note: splashing scatters things about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the city's letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A sweetheart on a Paris spree throwing money around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Honey' looks like a term of endearment; it is the rare word mel, Latin for honey and still used in pharmacy. Mellifluous shares the root.
explanation.definitionFit: The lempira is the currency of Honduras, so lempiras are cash in that country.

clue.text: Bishop behind everything and so very loud goes up in the air

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
what comes behind everything else is last
'and' joins; so is taken as written
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A bishop trailing behind everyone, making a din, rises skyward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes up in the air' might suggest losing your temper; here it is a rocket's launch.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket that blasts off leaves the ground on take-off, rising into the sky.

clue.text: The woman with an obsession offering protection

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
to have a thing about something is to be obsessed with it

explanation.surface: A woman with a fixation is looking out for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheathing is a protective covering, as on a ship's hull or a cable, so it shields what it encloses.

clue.text: Back of restaurant — competent server pouring out one drink

indicators.note: what is poured out is lost from the container, so a letter leaves the word
the back of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the last letter of restaurant
able means capable or competent
a waiter serves food and drink to diners
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: At the rear of a restaurant, a capable waiter is pouring someone a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: WAITER loses its I to become WATER. 'Pouring out' looks like serving the drink, but it removes a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Table water is bottled mineral water served at meals, so it is a drink.

clue.text: See 16
Sailor on his own gets food from the sea?

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
alone means by oneself

explanation.surface: A solitary sailor catches his own meal from the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Abalone is an edible sea snail prized as seafood, so it is food taken from the sea.

clue.text: Oh dear, cat wrecked geometrical shapes!

indicators.note: something wrecked is broken up, so these letters are smashed into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone groans as their cat smashes their collection of geometric models.
explanation.definitionFit: Octahedra, the plural of octahedron, are solid figures with eight faces, a family of geometrical shapes.

clue.text: A child that is on the street suffering most from exertion?

parts.note: taken as written
ch is the abbreviation for child
i.e. is Latin id est, that is
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A child out on the street is the most worn out after playing hard.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: aches come from exertion, among other causes.
explanation.definitionFit: Achiest is the superlative of achy, describing whoever hurts most, as after heavy exercise.

clue.text: Relative comfort, what a prisoner hopes for

parts.note: rel is the abbreviation for relative
ease is comfort or relief

explanation.surface: A jailed man's family brings some solace, though freedom is his real wish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relative comfort' reads as a phrase meaning moderate ease; split it into relative and comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Release is being set free from jail, the thing any inmate longs for.

clue.text: Seven Etonians excluding outsiders in Italian region

indicators.note: dropping the outer letters leaves a run from inside the words

parts.note: the run of letters from inside these words

explanation.surface: Seven old boys of Eton go on holiday to northern Italy, leaving out strangers.
explanation.definitionFit: Veneto is the region of north-east Italy whose capital is Venice.

clue.text: Most impulsive atheists being nasty

indicators.note: nasty suggests something turned bad or out of order, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A jibe that unbelievers are the most rash people when they turn spiteful.
explanation.definitionFit: Hasty means acting quickly without thought, so the hastiest people act on impulse more than anyone.

clue.text: Comb horse — starts to look elegant

parts.note: a hack is a horse for ordinary riding

indicators.note: starts are first letters, so only the opening letter of each following word is kept

parts.note: first letters of look and elegant

explanation.surface: Grooming advice: brush the horse's mane and it begins to look smart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comb' looks like an instruction to groom the horse, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackle is a steel-toothed comb for dressing flax, and to hackle is to comb flax with one.

clue.text: Caught a bird hiding in a tree

indicators.note: hiding the word in makes it vanish, so those two letters drop out

parts.note: c is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
taken as written
the robin is a common garden bird

explanation.surface: A bird is trapped after taking cover among branches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hiding in a tree' looks like where the bird is; 'hiding in' removes IN from ROBIN, and 'a tree' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The carob is a Mediterranean evergreen whose pods give a chocolate substitute.

clue.text: Phone in caravan?

parts.note: a mobile is a mobile phone
someone at home is in

explanation.walkthrough: 'Phone in' looks like a radio phone-in; it is two separate pieces. The question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravan is a trailer people live in when travelling, a home on wheels that can be moved.

clue.text: Heartless opponent making money

indicators.note: without its heart a word loses its central letter

parts.note: a rival is an opponent

explanation.surface: A cruel adversary turns a profit.
explanation.walkthrough: RIVAL has five letters, so its heart is the V in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The rial is the currency of Iran, Oman and Yemen, so it is a unit of money.

clue.text: Philosopher's bit of work absorbed by British disciple

indicators.note: what is absorbed is taken inside, so one piece goes within the others

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
an erg is a small unit of work in physics
a son can be a follower or disciple, as in a son of the prophets

explanation.surface: A philosopher's small task is taken up by an English follower.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'has', linking definition and wordplay; British and disciple together do the absorbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Bergson was a French philosopher, Nobel laureate, known for his ideas on time and intuition.

clue.text: After mad turns was first to be put in beastly home?

indicators.note: when something turns it faces the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy
to have led is to have been in front

explanation.surface: Someone who went crazy and came out ahead is locked up like an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly home' looks like an insult; it means a home for beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that is stabled has been put in a stable, the building where animals are kept.
